text: amphotericin B or caspofungin are usually effective but only indicated in pa- tients with refractory disease.1-3 Oral posaconazole was found to be as effective as oral fluconazole in the treatment of oropharyngeal candidiasis in HIV-infected persons, but more effective than fluconazole is sustaining clinical ben- efit after treatment was stopped.4 Oesophageal infections are not normally accessible to topical therapy and oral or intravenous fluconazole or itra- conazole are considered to be the drugs of choice. Severe or refractory disease may be treated with voriconazole, ei- ther intravenously or orally, or intravenous caspofungin or amphotericin B.1-3,5 Genital candidiasis responds well to topical antifungal treatment with creams or pessaries. Uncomplicated vagin- itis responds to short-course topical therapy with azoles such as butoconazole, clotrimazole, econazole, fenticona- zole, isoconazole, miconazole, terconazole, or tiocona- zole, to topical nystatin, or to oral therapy with fluconazole or itraconazole.6,7 Complicated disease, which occurs in up to 10% of cases, requires at least 7 to 14 days of treat- ment with topical antifungals or an oral dose of flucona- zole repeated 72 hours later.1,6 Vulvovaginal candidiasis with non-albicans species may not respond to topical azoles, in which case topical boric acid or topical flucyto- sine are often effective.1 In pregnancy, topical azoles are recommended6,7 and appear to be more effective than nys- tatin;8 treatment is given for 7 days. Recurrent vaginal can- didiasis should be treated for at least 6 months.6,7 In the USA,6 initial treatment with a topical or oral azole is rec- ommended. Some suggest that the duration of therapy be increased to 7 to 14 days for the topical products and that the oral dose of fluconazole may be repeated every 72 hours for a total of 3 doses. Recommended maintenance therapy is with oral fluconazole once weekly; alternative regimens are topical clotrimazole 200 mg twice weekly or 500 mg once weekly, or other topical treatments used in- termittently. UK guidelines7 recommend initial treatment with fluconazole 150 mg every 72 hours for 3 doses fol- lowed by maintenance treatment of 150 mg once weekly. Alternatively initial treatment may be with a topical azole product for 10 to 14 days, followed by maintenance with topical clotrimazole 500 mg once weekly, oral fluconazole 100 mg once weekly, or daily oral itraconazole or ketoco- nazole.
